spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m6p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
Rooms == {"o1","o2","o3"}
Cap == 2
T == 2
VARIABLES room, inUse
Init == room = [r \in Rooms |-> 0] /\ inUse = 0
Book(r) == room[r] = 0 /\ inUse < Cap /\ room' = [room EXCEPT ![r] = T] /\ inUse' = inUse + 1
Tick(r) == room[r] > 1 /\ room' = [room EXCEPT ![r] = room[r] - 1] /\ inUse' = inUse
Expire(r) == room[r] = 1 /\ room' = [room EXCEPT ![r] = 0] /\ inUse' = inUse - 1
Next == \E r \in Rooms : Book(r) \/ Tick(r) \/ Expire(r)
vars == <<room, inUse>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
CapacityNeverExceeded == inUse <= Cap /\ inUse = Cardinality({r \in Rooms : room[r] > 0})
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityNeverExceeded
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler manages three operating rooms that two scheduling instances share. Each booking takes a room under a lease with a countdown; the lease ticks down and, on the final tick, frees the room. To respect staffing limits, no more than a fixed capacity of rooms may be in use at once, so a booking is allowed only while occupancy is below capacity. An in-use counter is kept alongside the room timers. The requirement is that concurrent occupancy never exceeds the capacity and that the counter faithfully tracks how many rooms are actually occupied.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of occupied operating rooms never exceeds the capacity and always equals the tracked in-use count.

spec_text:

Vacate(p) == cleared[p] /\ version < MaxV /\ cleared' = [cleared EXCEPT ![p] = FALSE] /\ version' = version + 1 /\ admin' = admin
AdminClear == admin' = TRUE /\ cleared' = [p \in Planes |-> FALSE] /\ version' = version
Next == AdminClear \/ (\E p \in Planes : Clear(p) \/ Vacate(p))
vars == <<cleared, version, admin>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
OneRunwayUser == \A p1 \in Planes, p2 \in Planes : (cleared[p1] /\ cleared[p2]) => (p1 = p2)

cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OneRunwayUser
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator grants exclusive use of a single active runway to landing planes using optimistic version checks. A plane may take the runway only when no plane is currently cleared, and each grant or vacate bumps a version stamp used to detect and retry lost races. There is a privileged control-tower override that can force-clear the runway at any moment, wiping all clearances so the tower can reclaim it in an emergency. The essential safety requirement is mutual exclusion of the runway: two planes must never both hold clearance to the runway at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one plane is cleared for the runway in any reachable state.

spec_text:

AcquireFine == coarse /\ fine < cap /\ fine' = fine + 1 /\ coarse' = coarse /\ cap' = cap
ReleaseFine == fine > 0 /\ fine' = fine - 1 /\ coarse' = coarse /\ cap' = cap
ReleaseCoarse == coarse /\ fine = 0 /\ coarse' = FALSE /\ fine' = fine /\ cap' = cap
Reconfig == \E c \in {1, 2, 3} : c >= fine /\ cap' = c /\ coarse' = coarse /\ fine' = fine
Next == AcquireCoarse \/ AcquireFine \/ ReleaseFine \/ ReleaseCoarse \/ Reconfig
vars == <<coarse, fine, cap>>

cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator uses hierarchical locking: a controller must first take the coarse airspace lock before acquiring any fine per-runway slot, and it releases the coarse lock only after all fine slots are released. The number of fine slots that may be held at once is bounded by a capacity that can change at runtime as weather opens or closes runways, but a reconfiguration may never drop the capacity below the number of slots currently in use. The safety requirements are that held fine slots never exceed the current capacity and that no fine slot is ever held without the coarse airspace lock.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of held fine slots never exceeds the current capacity, and any held fine slot implies the coarse airspace lock is held.

spec_text:

Signals == {"s1","s2","s3"}

Leave(t) == inBlock[t] /\ inBlock' = [inBlock EXCEPT ![t] = FALSE] /\ votes' = votes
Next == (\E t \in Trains : Enter(t) \/ Leave(t)) \/ (\E s \in Signals : Vote(s))

cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BlockExclusion
nl:
A subway signalling block system grants a single track block to at most one train at a time, and a train may enter only after a quorum of interlocking signals approves the movement. Signals cast approval votes that can arrive reordered; once a quorum has voted and no train occupies the block, a train enters and the votes reset. A train leaves the block when its movement completes. The critical safety requirement is mutual exclusion of the block: two trains must never occupy the same block simultaneously.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one train occupies the track block in any reachable state.

cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next

nl:
A subway signalling block system tracks how many trains occupy each of two adjacent segments using a compare-and-swap register that mirrors the first segment's occupancy. A train moves from one segment to the other only by a successful compare-and-swap: the move proceeds when the register still equals the first segment's count, updating both the segment counts and the register together. A controller node may crash silently and simply stop issuing moves. Trains are conserved across the two segments, and the register must stay consistent with the first segment's true occupancy.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the two segment occupancies always sum to the fixed total, and the register always equals the first segment's occupancy.

cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PrintedAtMostOnce
nl:
A print shop spooler runs two independent token rings over the same pool of print jobs; each ring passes a single token from station to station, and only the station currently holding a ring's token is allowed to send a job to the press. Because a physical print is irreversible, each job must be sent to the press at most once even though two rings can both reach into the shared job pool. A ring advances its token cyclically among its stations, and either ring may print a job that has not yet been printed. The concern is that the two rings could both grab the same unprinted job and each send it to the press, printing it twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every job is sent to the press at most once across both token rings.

Next == \E m \in Machines : Read(m) \/ (\E s \in Slots : Purchase(m, s))

cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DispenseAtMostOnce
nl:
A vending machine network sells items from per-slot inventory across two machines that share a common catalog, using optimistic version checks. A machine reads the current catalog version, then completes a purchase of an item slot only if that slot has not already been vended and the version it read still matches; a purchase marks the slot vended and bumps the version. One machine may crash silently and simply stop transacting without harming the others. Dispensing an item is irreversible, so each slot must be vended at most once even under racing purchases from both machines.
SAFETY PROPERTY: every item slot is dispensed at most once across the network.

A wildfire drone surveillance swarm launches drones only after a quorum of the swarm's controllers approve, and it caps how many drones may be airborne at once to respect the operator's airspace limit. Controllers cast approval votes for a pending launch; approval messages can be reordered, so votes accumulate until a quorum is reached, at which point one drone launches and the votes reset. Airborne drones land one at a time. The requirement is that the number of airborne drones never exceeds the capacity cap.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of airborne drones never exceeds the airspace capacity cap.

spec_text:

Zones == {"z1","z2"}

AcquireRegion == ~regionLock /\ regionLock' = TRUE /\ droneLock' = droneLock /\ dropCount' = dropCount
AcquireDrone(d) == regionLock /\ droneLock = "none" /\ droneLock' = d /\ regionLock' = regionLock /\ dropCount' = dropCount
Drop(z) == droneLock # "none" /\ dropCount[z] = 0 /\ dropCount' = [dropCount EXCEPT ![z] = 1] /\ regionLock' = regionLock /\ droneLock' = droneLock
ReleaseDrone == droneLock # "none" /\ droneLock' = "none" /\ regionLock' = regionLock /\ dropCount' = dropCount
ReleaseRegion == regionLock /\ droneLock = "none" /\ regionLock' = FALSE /\ droneLock' = droneLock /\ dropCount' = dropCount

nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm uses hierarchical locking to control retardant drops: a drone must first take the coarse region lock, then acquire the single fine drop-authority lock before dropping over a zone. A retardant drop over a zone is irreversible, so each zone may be dropped on at most once. One drone may crash silently and simply stop, leaving the locks to be released by the protocol. The requirements are that no drop happens without holding the fine authority under the region lock, and that no zone is dropped on more than once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: each zone is dropped on at most once, and holding the fine drop-authority always implies the coarse region lock is held.

nl:
An airport baggage router moves bags between a check-in zone and a make-up zone, with a transit belt in between. A bag is picked from one zone onto the belt, then delivered off the belt into the other zone, and the same happens in reverse for rerouted bags. The router uses optimistic handling with retries, so a move that loses a race simply does nothing and is retried later, and a single conveyor node may crash silently and just stop contributing without corrupting anything. No matter how bags shuffle between the two zones and the belt, the total number of bags in the system is fixed: nothing is ever created or destroyed.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the total number of bags across the two zones and the transit belt is always equal to the fixed initial count.

Finalizing a book is irreversible, so it is appended to an ordered fulfillment log, and a book that already appears in the log may not be finalized again. A privileged head-librarian override can seize the token back to a default desk at any time. The concern is that a book could be finalized more than once and appear twice in the fulfillment log.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no book appears more than once in the fulfillment log.

Each lock is taken under a lease with an expiry timer; the timer ticks down and, once expired, one held lease is released. No matter how leases are acquired, tick, expire, or are admin-granted, the number of concurrently held leases must never exceed the hard ceiling.

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT AtMostOneActiveMatch
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker lets two clients contend for a single shared match server using optimistic locking. Each client first reads the current version stamp of the slot, then tries to claim the free slot only if the version it read still matches the live version; a successful claim bumps the version and marks a match active, while a stale read simply fails and the client retries. Reads and claim attempts from the two clients can be interleaved and effectively reordered. Releasing the slot also bumps the version. The invariant of interest is mutual exclusion of the match server: there can never be more than one active match at a time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of active matches on the shared server never exceeds one.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od5m2p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Integers
Lobbies == {"A","B"}
Players == {"p1","p2"}
VARIABLES phase, yesvotes, slot
Init == phase = [l \in Lobbies |-> "idle"] /\ yesvotes = [l \in Lobbies |-> {}] /\ slot = "free"
Prepare(l) == phase[l] = "idle" /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![l] = "preparing"] /\ yesvotes' = [yesvotes EXCEPT ![l] = {}] /\ slot' = slot
Vote(l, p) == phase[l] = "preparing" /\ p \notin yesvotes[l] /\ yesvotes' = [yesvotes EXCEPT ![l] = yesvotes[l] \cup {p}] /\ phase' = phase /\ slot' = slot
Commit(l) == phase[l] = "preparing" /\ yesvotes[l] = Players /\ slot = "free" /\ slot' = l /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![l] = "holding"] /\ yesvotes' = yesvotes
Release(l) == phase[l] = "holding" /\ slot = l /\ slot' = "free" /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![l] = "idle"] /\ yesvotes' = [yesvotes EXCEPT ![l] = {}]
Abort(l) == phase[l] = "preparing" /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![l] = "idle"] /\ yesvotes' = [yesvotes EXCEPT ![l] = {}] /\ slot' = slot
Next == \E l \in Lobbies : (Prepare(l) \/ Commit(l) \/ Release(l) \/ Abort(l) \/ (\E p \in Players : Vote(l, p)))
vars == <<phase, yesvotes, slot>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
MatchSlotExclusive == \A l1 \in Lobbies, l2 \in Lobbies : (phase[l1] = "holding" /\ phase[l2] = "holding") => l1 = l2
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MatchSlotExclusive
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker runs two competing lobbies, A and B, that each want to reserve the single shared match server slot for their group. Each lobby uses a two-phase commit: it prepares, then collects a yes vote from every player in its group before it may claim the slot. Player yes votes travel over the network and can arrive in any order, so a lobby accumulates them into a set until all players have voted. A lobby may commit and take the slot only when it has all its yes votes and the slot is currently free; when its match ends it releases the slot back to free. A half-prepared lobby may also abort and return to idle. The danger is that both lobbies could believe they own the match server at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at no reachable state are both lobbies in the holding phase owning the match server simultaneously.

nl:

A car acquires the shaft under a lease with a fixed expiry timer; the timer ticks down, and once it reaches zero and the car is not actively servicing, the lease expires and the shaft returns to free. A car may begin servicing only while it holds the lease, and there is a privileged building-admin override that can seize the shaft at any moment, forcing any current servicing to stop. The requirement is that two cars must never be servicing the shared shaft at the same time.
SAFETY PROPERTY: any car that is servicing the shaft must be the current lease owner, so no two cars service it at once.

spec_text:

Enroll == leader # "none" /\ available > 0 /\ available' = available - 1 /\ enrolled' = enrolled + 1 /\ leader' = leader

A university course-registration system runs with a single elected registrar leader that can fail over to a backup; two registrar instances share the same seat pool. Only the current leader may enroll or drop students, moving seats between available and enrolled. A failover clears the leadership so another registrar can be elected, but does not touch the seat counts. Whatever leader is active and however enrollments and drops interleave, the total number of seats is conserved: every seat is either still available or currently enrolled.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m4p2t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
Runways == {"r1","r2"}
N == 3
VARIABLES pending, runway, landed
Init == pending = 3 /\ runway = [r \in Runways |-> "free"] /\ landed = 0
Assign(r) == pending > 0 /\ runway[r] = "free" /\ runway' = [runway EXCEPT ![r] = "busy"] /\ pending' = pending - 1 /\ landed' = landed
Clear(r) == runway[r] = "busy" /\ runway' = [runway EXCEPT ![r] = "free"] /\ landed' = landed + 1 /\ pending' = pending
Depart == landed > 0 /\ landed' = landed - 1 /\ pending' = pending + 1 /\ runway' = runway
Next == Depart \/ (\E r \in Runways : Assign(r) \/ Clear(r))
vars == <<pending, runway, landed>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
FlightsConserved == pending + Cardinality({r \in Runways : runway[r] = "busy"}) + landed = N
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FlightsConserved
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator manages a pool of flights waiting to land on two shared runways. Flights sit in a bounded pending queue; a controller assigns a waiting flight onto a free runway, and later clears the runway once the flight has landed, marking it landed. Two controller instances share the same pool of runways and pending flights and coordinate over who assigns next. The queue provides backpressure so assignment stops when no runway is free. Regardless of the interleaving of assignments and clearances, every flight is accounted for exactly once: the total of still-pending, currently-on-a-runway, and already-landed flights never changes.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the pending count plus the number of busy runways plus the landed count always equals the fixed total number of flights.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od3m4p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers
MaxTx == 4
Cap == 2

Admit == admitted < MaxTx /\ (admitted - posted) < Cap /\ admitted' = admitted + 1 /\ posted' = posted /\ balance' = balance
Post == (admitted - posted) > 0 /\ posted' = posted + 1 /\ balance' = balance + 1 /\ admitted' = admitted

Next == Admit \/ Post \/ ResetBatch

NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
A bank's interbank settlement engine drains a batch of pending transfers into a shared account record. A feeder admits transfers into a bounded pending buffer, but only while the buffer has room, giving backpressure when settlement falls behind. A poster takes one admitted transfer at a time and applies it to the account balance. The poster can be slow and lag well behind admission, but it is never considered failed, so every admitted transfer is eventually applied exactly once and no update is silently dropped. The balance must therefore always equal the number of transfers that have actually been posted, and posted work can never run ahead of what was admitted.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the account balance always equals the count of posted transfers, which never exceeds the count admitted.

Each bay advances its own car one stage at a time, and every advance must be reflected in the shared total with no lost updates, even across reconfigurations. The requirement is that the shared total always equals the sum of the two bays' stage counts.

spec_text:

Init == blockOwner = [b \in Blocks |-> "none"] /\ vote = [c \in Controllers |-> "idle"] /\ pend = [c \in Controllers |-> "none"]
Prepare(c, b) == vote[c] = "idle" /\ blockOwner[b] = "none" /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![c] = "yes"] /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![c] = b] /\ blockOwner' = blockOwner
Commit(c) == vote[c] = "yes" /\ pend[c] # "none" /\ blockOwner[pend[c]] = "none" /\ blockOwner' = [blockOwner EXCEPT ![pend[c]] = c] /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![c] = "committed"] /\ pend' = pend
Release(c) == vote[c] = "committed" /\ blockOwner' = [blockOwner EXCEPT ![pend[c]] = "none"] /\ vote' = [vote EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"] /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![c] = "none"]

vars == <<blockOwner, vote, pend>>
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
NoDoubleShed == \A c1 \in Controllers, c2 \in Controllers : (vote[c1] = "committed" /\ vote[c2] = "committed" /\ pend[c1] = pend[c2]) => (c1 = c2)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleShed
nl:
A power-grid load shedder assigns load blocks to controllers using two-phase commit so a given block is shed by only one controller. A controller prepares by voting yes on a free block and recording it as its pending target; it then commits, taking ownership of that block only if it is still unowned. One controller may crash silently and simply stop before committing, leaving its vote outstanding. The danger is double allocation of the same block: two controllers both committing the same load block would double-shed it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no two distinct controllers are both committed on the same pending load block.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m2p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers
Slots == {"s1","s2"}
Parties == {"spooler","printer"}
VARIABLES slotState, votes, txSlot
Init == slotState = [s \in Slots |-> "none"] /\ votes = {} /\ txSlot = "none"
Begin(s) == txSlot = "none" /\ slotState[s] = "none" /\ txSlot' = s /\ votes' = {} /\ slotState' = slotState
Vote(p) == txSlot # "none" /\ p \notin votes /\ votes' = votes \cup {p} /\ txSlot' = txSlot /\ slotState' = slotState
Commit == txSlot # "none" /\ votes = Parties /\ slotState' = [slotState EXCEPT ![txSlot] = "held"] /\ txSlot' = "none" /\ votes' = {}
Abort == txSlot # "none" /\ txSlot' = "none" /\ votes' = {} /\ slotState' = slotState
Free(s) == slotState[s] = "held" /\ slotState' = [slotState EXCEPT ![s] = "none"] /\ txSlot' = txSlot /\ votes' = votes
Next == Commit \/ Abort \/ (\E s \in Slots : Begin(s) \/ Free(s)) \/ (\E p \in Parties : Vote(p))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A print shop job spooler commits a slot allocation using two-phase commit between the spooler and the printer: both parties must vote before a slot is finalized as held. A transaction begins against a free slot, then each party votes, and a commit occurs only once both have voted, marking the slot held. A participant can be slow but not failed, so the printer may vote well after the spooler. A transaction may only begin against a slot that is not already allocated. The concern is double allocation: an in-flight transaction must never target a slot that is already held.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a transaction is in flight, its target slot is not already allocated.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m5p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Integers, FiniteSets
Nodes == {"n1","n2","n3"}
Total == 3
Quorum == 2
VARIABLES stored, dispensed, votes
Init == stored = 3 /\ dispensed = 0 /\ votes = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]
CastVote(n) == votes[n] = FALSE /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![n] = TRUE] /\ stored' = stored /\ dispensed' = dispensed
Dispense == Cardinality({n \in Nodes : votes[n]}) >= Quorum /\ stored > 0 /\ stored' = stored - 1 /\ dispensed' = dispensed + 1 /\ votes' = [n \in Nodes |-> FALSE]
Restock == dispensed > 0 /\ dispensed' = dispensed - 1 /\ stored' = stored + 1 /\ votes' = votes
Next == Dispense \/ Restock \/ (\E n \in Nodes : CastVote(n))

BloodConserved == stored + dispensed = Total

NEXT Next
INVARIANT BloodConserved
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker requires a quorum of custody nodes to approve each unit dispensed from a shared cold store. Nodes cast approval votes for the pending dispense; once a quorum of them has voted, one unit moves from stored to dispensed and the votes reset for the next action. A participant node can be slow but not failed, so it may lag in voting while a quorum still forms from the others. Blood units are neither created nor destroyed by tracking: every unit is either still stored or already dispensed. The requirement is conservation of the total unit count at all times.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of stored units plus the number of dispensed units always equals the fixed initial total.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m9p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Rx == {"x1","x2"}
MaxEpoch == 2
VARIABLES allocs, epoch

Allocate(s, r) == (\A p \in allocs : p[1] # s) /\ allocs' = allocs \cup {<<s, r>>} /\ epoch' = epoch
Free(s) == (\E p \in allocs : p[1] = s) /\ allocs' = {p \in allocs : p[1] # s} /\ epoch' = epoch
Reconfig(s) == epoch < MaxEpoch /\ epoch' = epoch + 1 /\ allocs' = {p \in allocs : p[1] # s}

NoDoubleAllocation == \A p1 \in allocs, p2 \in allocs : (p1[1] = p2[1]) => (p1[2] = p2[2])
====
cfg_text:

NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser assigns physical medication bins (slots) to prescriptions. Two dispenser instances share the same pool of bins, each recording assignments as slot-to-prescription pairs. Periodically the system performs an epoch-numbered reconfiguration: it bumps the epoch and frees a chosen bin, clearing whatever prescription was assigned to it so it can be reused. A dispenser may assign a prescription to a bin only if that bin is not already assigned. The safety concern is that the same bin could end up allocated to two different prescriptions at once, which would misroute medication.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no bin is ever recorded as allocated to two different prescriptions at the same time.

A participant can be slow but is not failed, so a prepared reservation may wait before committing, and different members may prepare against different copies. The safety concern is double allocation of the same slot: no single copy may end up committed to two different members.
